exercise.name: Band Incline Bench Press
aliases: Incline band chest press on a bench

reference.title: Band Incline Bench Press
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the data sheet was not read; the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the band draws the hands down, exhale as you press up against it.
breathing.cadence: About 2.0 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.2 s up

prescription.tempo: 2-0-1-0 (2 s down, no pause, 1 s up)
prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen (bands are colour-coded by tension): pick one you can move for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve; stand or sit farther from the anchor, or choke up on the band, for more tension.
prescription.progression: More reps, a slower return, more distance from the anchor (more stretch), then the next band up.

cues.text: Set a rack (or two sturdy uprights) just behind the top of the bench and loop a band around each upright low down. Back pad at 30 degrees; glutes in the crease, upper back and head on the pad, feet planted; a handle in each hand, arms straight over the upper chest, palms toward the feet.
Breathe in and let the band draw the hands down slowly, elbows about 45-60 degrees from your sides, forearms vertical.
Hands beside the upper chest, upper arms just below the bench line; keep the band taut, no slack.
Breathe out and press up and slightly in against the band until the arms are straight over the shoulders.
Hold the top for a moment with the shoulder blades still pinned back, then lower again.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flared straight out at 90 degrees (a "T")
mistakes.fix: Bring the elbows to about 45-60 degrees from the body; the band strands then run past the outside of the elbows.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band snap the hands back down
mistakes.fix: Lower for about 2 s and keep tension at the bottom.

mistakes.mistake: Wrists bent back by the band
mistakes.fix: Keep the knuckles up and the wrists straight over the forearms.

mistakes.mistake: Shoulders rolling forward off the pad at the top
mistakes.fix: Reach only until the arms are straight; keep the shoulder blades on the pad.

mistakes.mistake: Sliding down the bench as the band pulls
mistakes.fix: Sit back into the crease and keep the feet planted.

kinematics.norm: Back pad at 30 degrees, seat flat. 30 degrees gave the highest upper-pectoralis activity; above it the anterior deltoid took over (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020, barbell, 0-60 degrees); Lauver 2016 recommends 30 degrees with the flat bench
Arms straight but not locked at the top; at the bottom the hands reach the sides of the chest with the elbows at roughly 90-110 degrees (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Elbow flare (upper arm from the trunk)
kinematics.norm: About 45-60 degrees from the body at the bottom, not a 90-degree "T" (clinical opinion)
Upper arms reach about level with, or a little below, the back (clinical opinion)

Forearms vertical under the hands; the hands rise and come slightly together over the shoulders while the band stretches (clinical opinion). Elastic resistance can reach muscle activity comparable to free weights (Andersen 2010, shoulder exercises; Calatayud 2015, band push-ups vs bench press)
Feet flat on the floor with the knees bent about 90 degrees, like the bench set-up in Solstad 2020 (head, shoulders and hips on the bench, about 90 degrees of knee flexion)
Controlled: about 2 s down and 1-2 s up. Rodríguez-Ridao 2020 used 2 s down and 2 s up at 60% of 1RM

cautions: Check the band for nicks or tears before every session and replace a worn band; a band that snaps can hit the face or eyes.
Anchor the band to something that cannot move or slip (a rack upright, a heavy bench frame or under the feet) and make sure it is secure before loading it.
Band tension rises as it stretches, so the load is lightest at the start and heaviest at the end of the push; let it return under control rather than snapping back.
Shoulder pain: shorten the range at the bottom until it settles (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight over the forearms.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: use a neutral grip (palms facing each other) and tuck the elbows a little more (band incline hammer press).
Too much tension at the top: use a lighter band or move the bench closer to the rack.
regressions: Lighter band, or a floor press with a band.
progressions: Stronger band or the bench moved farther from the rack.
Slower lowering (3-4 s) with a pause at the bottom.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pusher, with a shift toward the upper (clavicular) fibres: a 30-degree incline gave the highest upper-pectoralis activity, while the middle and lower fibres fell as the bench was raised (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020, barbell); Lauver 2016 also recommends a 30-degree incline for the pectoralis major.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Main pusher, with a shift toward the upper (clavicular) fibres: a 30-degree incline gave the highest upper-pectoralis activity, while the middle and lower fibres fell as the bench was raised (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020, barbell); Lauver 2016 also recommends a 30-degree incline for the pectoralis major.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Works harder as the bench rises: at 30 degrees it was about as active as the upper chest, and it became the most active muscle at 45 and 60 degrees (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Works harder as the bench rises: at 30 degrees it was about as active as the upper chest, and it became the most active muscle at 45 and 60 degrees (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbows; triceps activity did not change with bench angle (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020) and is lower with dumbbells than with a barbell (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbows; triceps activity did not change with bench angle (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020) and is lower with dumbbells than with a barbell (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage while each arm moves on its own.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage while each arm moves on its own.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Works as a stabiliser: biceps activity rose with the stability demand, highest with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Works as a stabiliser: biceps activity rose with the stability demand, highest with dumbbells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm while the band handles move freely (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm while the band handles move freely (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blades drawn back and down on the bench.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Keep the shoulder blades drawn back and down on the bench.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the ribs down and the pelvis on the seat.
